text: The name is meant: the function generates integers of any size (even integers between a and b), which contradicts the docstring's 'even digits' (contradiction with R-RET-2).
Used loosely for non-negative: a >= 0 and b >= 0; calls with 0 must also satisfy every other requirement.
a <= b is implicitly assumed: a call with a > b is outside the precondition and its behaviour is unconstrained.
Any collection of the values is acceptable (a list, tuple, set, generator, ...).
'Digits' is used loosely for numbers: every element is an even integer of any size, as the function name generate_integers suggests (contradiction with R-IF-2).
Exclusive: only values strictly greater than the lower bound and strictly less than the upper bound lie between a and b.
Ordered: the range runs from a up to b, so nothing lies between them when a > b and the list is empty.
Even integers of any size, as the function name generate_integers suggests: each element itself lies between a and b.
Exclusive: a and b themselves never appear; only values strictly between them are required.
Ordered: the even digits from a up to b must appear; nothing is required when a > b.
Every even integer of any size between a and b must appear, as the function name generate_integers suggests (contradiction with R-IF-2).
One entry per occurrence (for instance per occurrence of a digit in the decimal writing of the numbers between a and b): duplicates are allowed or required.
Ascending order is implied, as is conventional for a list of numbers in a range.
